findings.issue: ut5's scanner takes `site = min(at for _w, at in what)` as the function's first site, but no planted function has two sites with an ask between them. A function that asks after its first removal and before its second would be flagged now; mutating `min` to `max` (or any later site) would leave every planted case unchanged, so the first-site rule has no case that fails. Read from the source, not run. Likewise, `all(asks(...) for c in up)` is only pinned with a single caller (`late_inner` has one: `late_outer`). Nothing separates 'every caller' from 'any caller'.
findings.resolution: Add two planted twins. (a) A function with `run(['worktree','remove',a])`, then `tree_unsettled`, then a second removal, which must be named. (b) A remover with two callers, one asking before its call and one after, which must be named.
